note: Tuesday 07:00 SGT, pre-Asia-open, after the Mon 27 Jul US close. The regime-relevant shift held and extended: the US-Iran strike pause reached a THIRD straight night and the oil premium collapsed — Brent -8.7% to ~$88.36, WTI -7.5% to ~$82.61 — relieving the rate-hike fear that had pressured metals/REITs/crypto. Silver rebounded +2.3% to ~$59.4 (first up day/week/month/year since May), gold firmed to ~$4,098, crypto caught the bid (ETH +4.4%). US equities mixed at records: S&P +0.02% to 7,413, Dow +0.51% on the oil retreat, Nasdaq -0.18% on NVDA -5% and SanDisk -11% (the AI-capex/semis unwind persists). HY OAS ~269bp tight. Sentiment improved off Fear as risk relief spread (baked CNN ~44, crypto ~42 — the dashboard fetches Fear&Greed LIVE in-browser with these as fallback). Breadth & regional flows are researched (no free real-time API). CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run, so the 7 sub-components are INFERRED from the composite and cited internals and labeled as such. Flows carried from the EPFR/BofA week ending ~23 Jul (freshest weekly; not yet refreshed for the de-escalation).

components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index printed a fresh record close (~7,413, Mon 27 Jul) above a rising 125- and 200-DMA as the oil retreat eased inflation worries — momentum firmed back toward neutral. [Inferred — CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run]

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. Participation stayed broad (~69% of the S&P above its 200-DMA, best since February) but breadth momentum has stalled — balanced. [Inferred from exchange/Barchart data]

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). The NYSE McClellan Oscillator is hovering near zero and the Summation Index has rolled over since its 8 May peak (+471) — breadth thrust has faded to neutral. [Inferred — mcoscillator]

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options demand stayed on the hedged side through a jittery week of oil/rate/metals swings — a mildly fearful tilt consistent with the low-40s composite. [Inferred]

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. VIX closed ~18.6 on Fri 24 Jul — contained and near its 50-day average, not a panic reading; the least-fearful gauge. [VIX confirmed ~18.6 via Cboe/Yahoo]

components.name: Safe-Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Stocks held near highs while bonds sold off (10Y to a year-high ~4.71%) — bonds provided no haven bid, a modestly fearful mix. [Inferred]

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. HY OAS ~268bp stayed historically tight through the week — credit signals no stress, the most persistently greedy component. [FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 ~268bp]

breadth.note: Longer-term breadth is healthy but no longer broadening: ~69% of S&P members sit above their 200-DMA (best since February), yet the McClellan Oscillator is near zero and the Summation Index has rolled over since 8 May — indices hold near record highs (S&P 7,413) on narrower, stalling participation. The oil collapse eased the metals/rate stress that had hit Materials hardest, and Energy has now lost its war-premium leadership. Several sub-metrics (50-DMA %, daily A/D, net new highs, exact McClellan value) are approximate or lagged as labeled. The open question into the 29 Jul FOMC decision: whether a hawkish hold/hike re-tightens or a data-dependent Warsh confirms the risk relief.

flows.period: EPFR/BofA 'Flow Show' week ending ~23 Jul 2026 (freshest verifiable weekly), plus the July BofA Global Fund Manager Survey. Weekly flows lag ~2-6 days; this week now CAPTURES the front of the oil/rate/metals stress. Labeled week-to-23-Jul 2026.
flows.narrative: The freshest weekly read (to ~23 Jul) stayed net risk-on but rotated defensively: global equity funds drew +$30.4bn and bond funds +$14.9bn while money-market funds saw a large -$33.9bn outflow (cash being deployed, not hoarded). The standout was Financials: +$1.5bn on the week and a four-week cumulative +$8.8bn — the biggest four-week financials inflow since January 2022, consistent with the steeper curve and the sector's leadership. Gold funds added ~+$2.0bn and crypto ~+$0.9bn. BofA separately flagged China fuelling the second-largest weekly EM-equity inflow of the year — corroborating the HK/China-tech bid into the 24 Jul Politburo. Positioning remains the bigger tell: BofA's July FMS shows cash at just 3.6% of AUM (lowest since Feb), tripping the contrarian Cash-Rule SELL signal, with a net +42% equity overweight and a Bull & Bear Indicator at 9.5 (also a sell). Per-region Europe/Japan splits were not itemized in retrievable free sources this run.
